hero.headline: Pavel Skudarnov
hero.subtitle: Building modern web interfaces and production-ready applications with React, Next.js, and TypeScript.
hero.supporting: Handling frontend tasks from idea and UI to stable release: component architecture, responsiveness, performance, and polished user experience.

about.title: About Me
about.text: I am a frontend engineer who likes bringing interfaces to the point where they are not only good-looking, but genuinely comfortable to use. I work with React, Next.js, and TypeScript, build clear component structures, and pay close attention to responsiveness, states, forms, loading speed, and small UX details. In projects, I care about how the interface behaves with real data, errors, mobile screens, and future changes — not just how it looks in a clean mockup.

bullets: Develop landing pages, dashboards, and product interfaces for private projects and small business tasks.
Turn designs and ideas into working Next.js/React applications: pages, components, forms, loading states, and error states.
Polish projects to a production-ready level: responsive layouts, multi-language support, themes, basic SEO, and clear data structure.
Pay attention to product perception: copy, cards, empty states, micro-interactions, and mobile behavior.
Contributed to internal web platforms and interfaces for team workflows.
Built React components, pages, and backend API integrations while maintaining the existing frontend architecture.
Worked with SSR scenarios, interface states, forms, tables, and complex user flows.
Participated in code reviews, bug fixing, UI optimization, and preparing changes for release.
Helped make the UI more predictable: fewer edge-case bugs, clearer component behavior, and more stable user scenarios.
Started as a QA Engineer: checked requirements, wrote test scenarios, found defects, and reproduced edge cases.
Gradually moved into frontend development and helped maintain client-facing interfaces.
Worked with legacy code, helped migrate separate parts of the UI to React, and simplified page maintenance.
My QA background helps me treat frontend not only as markup, but as a product scenario with errors, constraints, and real users.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Portfolio projects where I show not only visuals, but real frontend scenarios: responsiveness, states, navigation, performance, and the feeling of a real product.

list.title: Frontend Portfolio
list.description: A personal website built as a clean experience showcase: not overloaded, easy to scan, available in two languages, and focused on quick access to projects and background.
implemented: Homepage with hero, experience, skills, projects, and contact section
RU/EN localization, responsive navigation, and subtle motion effects
Basic SEO setup: metadata, canonical, sitemap, and robots
decisions: Content is stored in dictionaries to keep two locales easy to maintain
The interface stays lightweight without unnecessary UI libraries or heavy dependencies
Page structure is designed for quick recruiter/client scanning
production: Accessible links, buttons, and clear interactive states
Deployment on a VPS behind nginx/PM2
list.impact: The site became a central point for resume, projects, and GitHub profile.

list.title: FlowPilot
list.description: A dashboard for analytics and workflow management. The focus is readable data, clear widgets, and an interface that stays usable across different screen sizes.
implemented: Dashboard pages with metrics, charts, and status cards
Responsive grid, sidebar navigation, and adaptive layout
Loading states, empty states, and fallback behavior
decisions: Charts are separated into reusable blocks to avoid duplicating display logic
Filters and interface states are kept predictable for future extension
The visual language is closer to a SaaS product than a static mockup
production: Error handling without empty broken screens
Optimized display of lists and cards on mobile devices
Checked readability of charts and metrics in dark/light environments
list.impact: The project demonstrates dashboard patterns, data states, and product analytics UI.

list.title: NordShop
list.description: An e-commerce showcase for a workspace goods brand. The project is not only about polished product cards, but about the whole shopping flow: catalog, filters, product page, and cart.
implemented: Homepage, catalog, filters, product cards, product details, and cart
RU/EN switching, dark/light theme, and responsive shopping flow
Toast notifications, loading/skeleton states, and polished cart states
decisions: The catalog is built around clear product cards and fast product selection
The cart is treated as part of the user journey, not just a separate screen
Visual presentation is pushed toward a premium storefront feel
production: Checked add-to-cart, quantity change, and cart clearing scenarios
Safe LocalStorage handling with fallback for invalid data
SEO metadata for pages and careful image handling
list.impact: The project demonstrates e-commerce UX, cart state handling, and attention to storefront details.

list.title: StayFinder
list.description: A booking interface for property search. The goal is to make the selection flow clear: search, filters, property cards, and fast access to details.
implemented: Search page, filters, property cards, and responsive results grid
Mobile-friendly selection flow with clear visual hierarchy
Redesign toward a calmer and more trustworthy travel experience
decisions: Filtering is handled on the client side so the interface reacts quickly to user actions
Property cards are built around price, location, benefits, and quick comparison
The design focuses on readability and trust rather than an overloaded travel visual
production: Checked empty result states and filter behavior
Optimized property images and grid behavior for mobile screens
list.impact: The project demonstrates marketplace/booking patterns and complex user choice flows.

list.title: DevDocs
list.description: A documentation website for a developer product. The main task is to explain the product quickly, provide clear navigation, and make technical content comfortable to read.
implemented: Documentation homepage, content sections, navigation, and readable typography
Fast access to key blocks and a clear page structure
Technical UI in the style of a modern SaaS/developer tooling product
decisions: Content is organized around quick user questions: what it is, how to start, where the API is
Typography and spacing are tuned for long reading, not just landing-page effect
Navigation stays visible without competing with the main content
production: Responsive sidebar menu and stable section structure
Code highlighting and readable technical blocks
Static page generation for fast loading
list.impact: The project demonstrates developer experience, documentation structure, and technical product presentation.

contact.title: Open for Work & Projects
contact.subtitle: If you need a frontend engineer for a product, MVP, storefront, or improvement of an existing UI, I can join and bring the interface to a clean release-ready state.
